newsitem.title: LEBANON: UNICEF, Lebanon sign accord to aid children.
newsitem.headline: UNICEF, Lebanon sign accord to aid children.

text.p: The Lebanese government and UNICEF on Tuesday signed a $17.5 million agreement under which the U.N. agency will provide health, education and basic social services to children in Lebanon for five years.

"The cooperation agreement is for the coming five years, 1997 to 2001," UNICEF representative in Lebanon Thomas Ekvall told reporters after signing the agreement with Foreign Minister Faris Bouez in Beirut.
"It involves programmes and projects in the fields of health, education and basic social services. The total amount of the programme is $17.5 million for the five-year period."

Ekvall said UNICEF -- the United Nations International Children's Emergency Fund -- used to have larger programmes in Lebanon but since the 1975-90 civil war, money available for Beirut had been decreasing because of a growing gross national product and declining child mortality.
"I think that instead of being seen as something negative, it should rather be seen as something positive because it is indicative of that the situation is improving," he added.
Ekvall said programmes would be implemented by relevant ministries and all children would be affected.
"For example, in our programme of immunisation we hope we will be able to immunise all children...and when we talk about education we hope all children will go to school," he said.
"Street children and working children are a major part of this programme."
